messages:
alice: Customer on iOS reported SSE stream truncates when they flip to phone hotspot (SSID change) mid‑stream. Happens reliably when hotspot enable + quick network switch. Sending repro and logs. @ben @jordan

ben: Thanks — can you drop the client log + SDK version? any pcap?

alice: Repro steps (straight from customer):
1) iPhone 14 Pro, iOS 17.2, Redwood JS SDK v2.3.1
2) Start a streaming completion over LTE (no wifi)
3) Turn on phone hotspot and immediately switch the device to that hotspot (SSID swap) within ~5s of stream start
4) Observe partial JSON chunk returned then socket close, client shows ECONNRESET and SDK does not retry

Logs from client:
```
[2024-10-18T13:02:23Z] INFO stream_start request_id=abc123 model=gpt-4o
[2024-10-18T13:02:29Z] WARN net: TCP FIN detected, bytes_sent=2345
[2024-10-18T13:02:29Z] ERROR stream_abort err=ECONNRESET partial_bytes=1204
```

carla: @alice can you attach the pcap? also token rotation timing?

alice: Token TTL was 60s, client refresh happens at 45s — but this reproduces without a refresh. Pcap uploaded: https://files.internal/pcaps/1742501234-hotspot-swap.pcap

jordan: Quick read: looks like a NAT rebinding + TCP teardown race. Server keeps writing after client TCP FIN, gets RST when client re-creates connection; net result = truncated payload emitted then close. Likely HTTP/2 stream shutdown on the client side.

jordan: Two broad mitigations:
- Server: add tiny grace window on write failure when request_id is seen again (allow dedupe/resume) or flush final chunk before hard close.
- Client: make SDK tolerate partial chunk + reconnect to request remainder (we don't have resumable streams yet).

ben: Customer is asking about billing — they say they were charged for a 71‑token completion but only got 40 tokens of text before truncation. Do we charge for emitted tokens or completed responses?

maya: We bill per token emitted. However we can issue a one‑off support credit if the customer was adversely affected. Need invoice id + raw response bytes to validate.

alice: Action items proposal:
- Ask customer for SDK version + pcap (done)
- Offer pro‑rata credit pending finops review (maya)
- Eng triage: small server patch to add 250ms grace on write errors or better handling of RST after FIN during active writes (jordan)
- Recommend customer try SDK v2.4 which includes keepalive tweaks that reduce frequency of midstream closes

carla: I'll open an internal incident and link the customer case (C-12345). tagging eng oncall.

jordan: For triage notes: attach server side logs around request_id=abc123 and netstack traces. Hypothesis: client closes TCP then immediately rebinds IP -> new connection shows SYN from same client within 30–200ms. Server thinks connection gone and any in‑flight buffers can cause RST. Short term we can: 1) buffer end-of-stream and ensure we write it atomically before closing; 2) detect quick reconnect with same request id and attempt idempotent replay if client signals resume.

alice: Customer-side workaround we suggested: avoid toggling hotspot during active stream, or bump token TTL to avoid token refresh during transition. They tried and saw fewer failures when they extended TTL.

ben: Is this something we should block a patch release for? severity: medium‑high for mobile customers.

jordan: I'll scope a small change (grace window + log correlation) — low risk, can ship in minor release. Will need SDK change for explicit resume protocol later.

maya: I'll prepare credit offer text and wait on invoice id.

carla: Incident created: INC-2024-789. Linking case C-12345 and pcap.

alice: Thanks team. Follow ups: @jordan do a short PR for the grace window, @maya send credit, @carla keep customer updated with repro status. :thumbsup:
